_comment: The failure catalog (docs/ROADMAP.md, slice 9a; src/systems/failures.gd). A failure is a part of a system that fails: 'system' is the runtime system's key (SimRuntime.SYSTEMS) and 'part' what its fail(part) takes. 'caution' is the caution and warning status light that comes on (CautionWarning.LIGHTS), with the trigger the CSM Apollo Operations Handbook, SM2A-03-BLOCK II-(1), pp. 2.10-5 to 2.10-8, gives it [published], and a failure no light shows the crew (slice 10c, the SCE's, which the ground sees) has none and an empty 'light'; 'effect' what the system does then, as the simulator models it; 'expect' a Bus check that holds once it has (after 200 s at most); 'procedure' the malfunction procedure's title in data/malfunctions.json; 'event' the mission event it fires, and 'call' the crew's words to Houston, where it has them. A mission arms its failures at a GET in its mission.json ('failures': [{id, get_s}]), or a time after one of its events ([{id, event, after_s}], slice 9d); the instructor's page on the wrist menu fails any of them at once. The launch vehicle's failures (vehicle 'lv', slice 9d) light the main display console's launch vehicle lights ('lamp', its channel, and 'light') instead of a caution light; 'launch' is what the ground does about a failure in the launch: 'abort' ends it in the abort mode the flight is in, 'return' brings the crew home at once (mode III rather than IV). The LM's failures (vehicle 'lm', slice 9e) light the LM's caution and warning lights (LmCautionWarning.LIGHTS), with the triggers of the LM Apollo Operations Handbook, LMA790-3-LM, section 2.9.4 [published], and open their procedures in data/lm_malfunctions.json, in the LM's checklist book.

failures.title: Cryogenic oxygen tank 2
failures.effect: The tank vents in about three minutes; the shared valve module starves fuel cells 1 and 3, and tank 1 leaks away over 2 h 20 min
failures.call: Houston, we've had a problem. Main B bus undervolt; O2 tank 2 pressure reading zero.
failures._comment: Apollo 13's, at 55:54:53 (MSC-02680, Table 3-I) [published]: Eps.fail_o2_tank(2) [derived, the class's comment]. CRYO PRESS lights with an O2 tank below 800 psia. In the launch the ground brings the crew home at once, rather than into orbit ('launch': 'return', mode III late in the launch) [estimated: the flight rules aren't at hand]

failures.title: Fuel cell 1
failures.effect: The cell stops making power; the other two carry the load
failures._comment: FC 1 lights for a fuel cell's flow, temperature or pH out of limits [published]; the failure is the cell's [simplified: its output at once to nothing]

failures.title: Fuel cell 2
failures.effect: The cell stops making power; the other two carry the load

failures.title: Fuel cell 3
failures.effect: The cell stops making power; the other two carry the load

failures.title: SM RCS quad A
failures.effect: The quad's helium fails, its propellant pressure falls and its jets stop: pitch and Z translation on quad C alone
failures.procedure: Malfunction: SM RCS A, B, C or D
failures._comment: SM RCS A lights with the quad's secondary fuel pressure below 145 psia [published]; the failure is its helium's [simplified: the pressure and the jets gone at once]

failures.title: SM RCS quad B
failures.effect: The quad's helium fails, its propellant pressure falls and its jets stop: yaw and Y translation on quad D alone
failures.procedure: Malfunction: SM RCS A, B, C or D

failures.title: SM RCS quad C
failures.effect: The quad's helium fails, its propellant pressure falls and its jets stop: pitch and Z translation on quad A alone
failures.procedure: Malfunction: SM RCS A, B, C or D

failures.title: SM RCS quad D
failures.effect: The quad's helium fails, its propellant pressure falls and its jets stop: yaw and Y translation on quad B alone
failures.procedure: Malfunction: SM RCS A, B, C or D

failures.title: The CMC
failures.effect: The computer stops: its DSKY goes dark, its autopilot and programs stop, and its IMU is caged
failures._comment: CMC lights for a loss of the CMC's prime power, among others [published]; the failure is the power's [simplified: for good, the IMU caged with it as a power-down cages it]

failures.title: The IMU
failures.effect: The platform fails and is caged: NO ATT on the DSKY, and no coarse align, P51 or P52 brings it back
failures._comment: ISS lights for an IMU failure, a gimbal's servo error over 2.9 mr for 2 s among them [published]

failures.title: The fuel cells' overload sensors
failures.effect: A transient trips every fuel cell on line off its buses: FC 1 to 3 and FC BUS DISCONNECT light, and the entry batteries carry the main buses under their undervolt limit until each cell's FC switch goes OFF and ON again
failures._comment: Apollo 12's first lightning strike, at 36.5 s: the transient on the battery relay bus fired the fuel cells' overload sensors' rectifiers and the three cells' motor switches opened in 0.1 s (MSC-01540, pp. 18 to 20); the mains fell to about 24 V on entry batteries A and B, and the crew put fuel cells 1 and 2 back on line at 142.5 s and 3 at 170.5 s (M-932-69-12, p. 15) [published]. The lights, FC 1 to 3 and FC BUS DISCONNECT among them (MSC-01855, section 9.2) [published]

failures.title: The SCE's NORM supply
failures.effect: The signal conditioning equipment drops out: the ground's telemetry reads nonsense (TM LOST) until SCE PWR goes to AUX. No light: Houston calls it
failures._comment: Apollo 12's first lightning strike dropped the SCE out (MSC-01855, section 7.2.1; M-932-69-12, p. 15) [published]; EECOM's 'SCE to AUX' at 1:36, the crew's switch to it at 1:50 on the onboard tape (the Apollo Flight Journal) [published]. The SCE has no caution light: the ground sees its telemetry go, the crew nothing

failures.title: The IMU's platform tumbled
failures.effect: A transient drives the platform's gimbals round and its orientation is lost: ISS and NO ATT, the platform caged until a coarse align; P51 aligns it again
failures._comment: Apollo 12's second lightning strike, at 52 s: the CDUs' readings jumped past 85 deg, the CMC switched the platform to coarse align, and in the launch's configuration its loop drove the gimbals round at about 35 deg/s (MSC-01540, pp. 21 to 23) [published]; the ISS light at about 50 s (MSC-01855, section 9.2), and P51 in the parking orbit's first night (ibid., section 9.3) [published]

failures.title: The docking probe's capture latches
failures.effect: The probe's three capture latches don't engage the drogue, and each contact rebounds. Held in the drogue under +X and retracted (PROBE RETRACT), the probe pulls the docking rings together to the twelve ring latches: hard dock, which clears it. No light: the crew sees the probe come back out
failures._comment: Apollo 14's, at transposition and docking: five attempts, eight contacts from 3:13:53.7 to 4:32:29.3, without capture, the capture latches' plunger most probably held by debris; the sixth, at 4:56:44.9, held under +X for 14.3 s with the probe's retraction begun 6.9 s after contact, docked hard with the first ring latch's firing 11.8 s after contact. The mechanism worked normally at the lunar orbit's undocking and docking (MSC-04112, section 14.1.1 and p. 7-1) [published]. The mission's timeline has it at CSM/LV SEP.

failures.title: A main parachute
failures.effect: One of the three mains deflates to a fifth of its diameter, out or as it comes out: the cluster keeps two's drag, and the CM comes down at about 36 ft/s at the water against three's 32, within the design. No light: the crew and the recovery forces see it
failures._comment: Apollo 15's: one of its mains deflated to about a fifth of its diameter at about 6,000 ft, some 99 s after they came out, two or three of its six riser legs gone, most probably burnt by the raw fuel the CM RCS's depletion firing was dumping, and the CM came down on two at about 37.5 ft/s from there (MSC-05161, section 14.1.9; MSC-05805) [published; the rate derived]. The mission's failures arm it 99 s after the mains come out.

failures.title: S-IC engine 1
failures.effect: The F-1 shuts down: its LV ENG light comes on and the S-IC burns on the others. With a second out the EDS aborts
failures.procedure: Malfunction: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID
failures._comment: Slice 9d's launch vehicle failures have no caution and warning light but the main display console's launch vehicle lights (lamp, light) [published: CSM Apollo Operations Handbook, section 2.9.4.5.2]; 'launch' says the ground ends the launch for them (MissionSequencer's aborts). S-IC engines 1 and 2 stand for any two of its five [simplified]: the vehicle flies on with one out, and both out is the EDS's two-engines-out abort

failures.title: S-IC engine 2
failures.effect: The F-1 shuts down: its LV ENG light comes on and the S-IC burns on the others. With a second out the EDS aborts
failures.procedure: Malfunction: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID

failures.title: The IU's guidance platform
failures.effect: The IU loses its attitude reference and turns the vehicle away: LV GUID, and LV RATE through the S-IC's flight, where the EDS aborts on the rates
failures.procedure: Malfunction: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID
failures._comment: LV GUID lights for the IU's platform's loss of attitude reference, with LV RATE through the first stage's boost (section 2.9.4.5.2) [published]

failures.title: The S-II's centre engine
failures.effect: The centre J-2 shuts down: its LV ENG light comes on and the S-II burns on its four outboard engines, longer, the IU's guidance steering on what they give and the S-IVB burning longer to orbit
failures.procedure: Malfunction: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID
failures._comment: Apollo 13's (slice 10d): pogo, the S-II's 14 to 16 Hz oscillations diverging through the centre engine's LOX feed, tripped its thrust OK pressure switches and shut it down at 330.65 s, 132 s before the IU's planned cutoff; the IU's iterative guidance burned the four outboard engines about 34 s longer and the S-IVB about 9 s longer, and put the stack in its parking orbit (Saturn V launch vehicle flight evaluation report, AS-508, MPR-SAT-FE-70-2, sections 6.3, 8.2.3.2 and 9.3; Apollo 13 Mission Report, MSC-02680, section 4.0) [published]. Its light stays on until the S-II's separation [estimated: the flight manual's account of the lights, MSFC-MAN-508, section III]. The call is Lovell's (Apollo Flight Journal, 000:05:32) [published]

failures.title: The S-II's engines
failures.effect: All five J-2s shut down: the stack coasts on its S-II short of orbit until the crew aborts
failures.procedure: Malfunction: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID

failures.title: The S-IVB's engine
failures.effect: The J-2 shuts down short of orbit: mode IV takes the CSM on into orbit on the SPS
failures.procedure: Malfunction: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID
failures._comment: Apollo 11's alternate mission 1: the S-IVB failing before insertion, the CSM's contingency orbit insertion on the SPS (press kit) [published]

failures.title: The descent engine's helium regulator
failures.effect: The regulator fails closed: the descent tanks' pressure falls as the engine burns, and its thrust dies away with it; in the descent the crew abort stage
failures._comment: DES REG lights for the helium downstream of the regulators below 219.2 or above 259.1 psia, before staging, once the descent engine has first been armed [published]; the pressure's fall and the thrust's [estimated] (spacecraft.json "dps")

failures.title: LM RCS system A's regulator
failures.effect: System A's helium pressure goes out of limits and its jets stop: the LM flies on system B's; closing A's main shutoff valves puts the light out
failures.procedure: Malfunction: RCS A or B REG
failures._comment: RCS A REG lights for system A's helium above 218.8 or below 164.4 psia, and goes out when its main shutoff valves close [published]; the jets stop at once [simplified]

failures.title: LM RCS system B's regulator
failures.effect: System B's helium pressure goes out of limits and its jets stop: the LM flies on system A's; closing B's main shutoff valves puts the light out
failures.procedure: Malfunction: RCS A or B REG

failures.title: The LGC
failures.effect: The computer stops: its DSKY goes dark and its autopilot and programs stop; with GUID CONT at AGS the AGS holds the LM and the light goes out
failures._comment: LGC lights for the LGC's power failure among others, unless GUID CONT is at AGS [published]

failures.title: The LM's IMU
failures.effect: The LGC's platform fails and is caged: NO ATT on the DSKY; with GUID CONT at AGS the AGS holds the LM and the light goes out
failures._comment: ISS lights for a failure in the inertial subsystem, unless GUID CONT is at AGS [published]

failures.title: The ABORT pushbutton's contacts to the LGC
failures.effect: A particle in the switch shorts its contacts to the LGC: channel 30 shows ABORT set with the pushbutton out, and once the descent engine is lit P70 aborts the landing. A tap on the panel beside it, or the pushbutton's press, clears it; it comes back. No light: Houston sees it on the downlink
failures._comment: Apollo 14's: a command to abort on the descent engine detected at the LGC's input channel, not at the AGS or the descent engine's control assembly, at 104:16:07 and three more times, each removed by tapping on the panel near the switch; most probably metallic contamination in its hermetically sealed case, solder or stud slivers up to 0.030 in (MSC-04112, section 14.2.2) [published]. The mission's timeline has it at the flown times (Failures.recur()).

failures.title: The landing radar's range scale
failures.effect: The radar's range scale switches to low with nothing measured, where its trackers acquire the range only within 3,500 ft and the velocity within about 4,600 ft of altitude; with no range to measure it can't switch back, and ALT and VEL stay on through the braking phase. Cycling its breaker, PGNS: LDG RDR, brings it back in high scale, its data good some 20 s on. No light of its own: ALT and VEL, which data out of range light too
failures._comment: Apollo 14's: the scale switched to low at 107:57:34.66, 4 min 52 s before PDI, at a slant range of 63,000 ft with a beam-4 velocity of 3,000 ft/s at 35.4 deg incidence, beyond the range the design covers, where low-level noise can switch it; the breaker was cycled at Houston's call at 108:08:50.66 and the data came good 20 and 22 s later (MSC-04112, section 14.2.4 and Table 8-V) [published]. The mission's timeline has it at the flown time.
